source_snapshot.procedure: Provide an HTTP image URL, access the OpenBMC remote console/web GUI, activate and mount virtual media from network or local browse, then optionally enter the ISO to perform actions such as OS installation.
source_snapshot.criteria: Remote Console connects successfully; the CD-ROM mounts to the server and an Auto-install program appears under the server system.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek performs a state-changing web mount and checks lsblk/dmesg, but does not resolve whether auto-install must merely appear or actually run, protect disks/boot state, establish image integrity/transport policy or guarantee cleanup.

original_test_intent.purpose: At minimum, validate BMC remote-console access and HTTP virtual-media attachment such that the approved image is mounted and visible to the host as CD/DVD media; the source does not unambiguously define whether displaying or launching an auto-install program is also required.
original_test_intent.target: The exact BMC virtual-media CD/DVD instance and isolated server OS/boot environment, using an owner-approved immutable image URI; any installer target disk is undefined and cannot be inferred.
original_test_intent.scope: Remote-console connection, remote-media attachment, host visibility/content access and clean ejection are the safe reversible scope. Booting the media, launching an installer or modifying disks is a distinct destructive scope that remains unresolved by the source.
original_test_intent.operation: Preserve BMC/host/boot/storage baselines, verify the exact image URI/hash/transport and virtual-media capability, attach the media through the approved BMC flow with write protection where supported, prove BMC inserted state plus host device/content visibility, stop before autorun/boot/install, eject/deactivate and verify cleanup unless the owner supplies a separate explicit installation contract.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One attach/verify/eject cycle. No reboot, boot-from-media or installation duration/iteration is specified.
original_test_intent.expected_result: For the mount-only interpretation, remote console connects, the exact image is inserted and host-visible/readable as the expected optical/block device, no boot/storage mutation occurs, and ejection removes it cleanly. The additional auto-install acceptance remains undefined.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/BMC/virtual-media capability, isolated host boot/storage baseline, immutable image URI metadata/hash/certificate/auth policy, BMC remote-console and inserted/write-protected state, before/after host device and media-content identity, absence of unauthorized installer/boot/write activity, ejection and final health.
ambiguities: The procedure presents OS installation as an optional example, while the criterion requires an `Auto-install program` to appear; it does not define whether appearance, launch or completion is expected.
No target disk, data-loss boundary, unattended-install configuration, boot transition, reboot authorization or installation acceptance is defined.
The source mixes an HTTPS example with an HTTP template and provides no certificate, authentication, immutable-content or hash policy.
Steps combine network URI mounting and local Browse upload flows without saying which mechanism this HTTP case must validate.
source_conflicts: Procedure step 7 says the mounted ISO can be used for actions such as OS installation, but the criterion makes an undefined Auto-install program appearance mandatory; these imply materially different reversible versus destructive end states.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly keeps the whole testcase BLOCKED because mount-only versus auto-install changes purpose, blast radius and completion, not merely a parameter. It defines a safe reversible substage and prevents boot/install. V3 accepts the classification and makes the source conflict plus partial-safe-work boundary explicit.

applicable_history.decision: The historical review treats the action as a partial web mount and host lsblk check, but does not resolve the criteria's auto-install requirement.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Maintain BLOCKED for the complete testcase because its procedure and criterion conflict on mount-only versus installer behavior. Safe capability discovery and read-only baselines may proceed, but even a successful media mount cannot be declared completion until the owner resolves the end state.

available_now: The reversible remote-console and virtual-media attachment portion is technically understandable.
Read-only capability discovery, current virtual-media state and host boot/storage baselines can be collected without inserting media.
DMTF Redfish defines InsertMedia as attaching remote media and EjectMedia as detaching it; mounted/visible state is distinct from any OS installation action.
missing_inputs: Owner decision: mount-and-read only, display installer UI without launch, boot from media, start unattended installation or complete installation
If beyond mount-only: exact boot method, target disk/allowlist, data-loss approval, installer configuration, network/credential/secrets handling, completion and recovery
Exact BMC-supported network-versus-upload flow, immutable HTTP(S) URI/image/hash/type/size, certificate/auth policy and expected virtual CD/device/content identity
Isolation, console/OOB access, cleanup/eject policy, manual operator and approval gates
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The test/OS deployment owner resolves the intended end state and installation boundary; the BMC/platform owner supplies the supported virtual-media procedure; security/network owners approve transport/image provenance; the storage/system owner controls any boot/install target and data-loss authority.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Discover BMC virtual-media resources/capabilities, current inserted state and remote-console reachability without issuing Insert/Activate; capture host block/mount/boot inventory and BMC/OS health without clearing logs
Validate candidate image hash/type/size and URI certificate/access metadata offline, with secrets redacted; prepare a mount-only comparison and eject plan without submitting the URI
prohibited_until_closed: Do not insert/mount the example or any image, change boot order, reboot, launch autorun/installer, expose URI credentials, write any disk or claim testcase completion while the end-state conflict remains
Do not combine local upload and network URL flows, use mutable unauthenticated content, accept device appearance without image identity, or leave virtual media inserted
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: A source-owner decision replaces the conflict with one explicit terminal state; the run card selects one supported transport/flow, fixes image identity and host evidence, and—if installation is intended—adds target-disk allowlisting, data-loss approval, boot/install/recovery and completion criteria.

revision_candidate.test_name: BMC HTTP Virtual Media Attachment and Host Visibility — Intent Decision Required
revision_candidate.purpose: Pending owner decision: validate reversible HTTP virtual-media attachment/visibility, or define a separate authorized boot/install workflow. Do not infer installation from media mounting.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: An isolated test server and exact BMC release with a documented network virtual-media flow, approved remote console, immutable HTTP(S) image, host read-only device access and independent BMC/OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Safe provisional scope is one virtual CD/DVD attach, host visibility/content identity and eject cycle. Booting, autorun and OS installation remain out of scope until explicitly specified and approved.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Owner end-state decision; supported BMC network-media procedure; exact URI/image/hash/type/size and TLS/auth policy; expected BMC/media/host identity; isolation, console/OOB and cleanup; if installation is required, target disk, data-loss approval, installer configuration, boot path, completion and recovery.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: After the conflict is resolved, capture baselines, verify image provenance and selected transport, attach through the approved BMC mechanism with write protection where supported, confirm inserted state and exact host-visible media/content, perform only the approved terminal action, eject/deactivate and verify final host/BMC state.
revision_candidate.preconditions: One unambiguous end state and one transport path approved; isolated SUT; exact immutable image verified; secrets protected; virtual-media state clean; host boot/storage baseline and target protection ready; console/OOB and eject/recovery available; approval appropriate to any destructive scope.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Owner intent decision; BMC/version/capability; image URI metadata/hash and security policy; remote-console and insert state; exact virtual device/content identity; no unauthorized boot/write; terminal-state evidence; eject/cleanup; final host/BMC/boot/storage health.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact BMC vendor virtual-media procedure and owner-approved test end state; DMTF Redfish VirtualMedia semantics may be used only when implemented by this BMC and do not authorize installation.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never infer install authority from mount authority, use example/mutable/unverified media, place secrets in evidence, alter boot/storage, launch an installer, write an unallowlisted disk or leave media inserted after a mount-only test.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: BMC/system owner approves media insertion and cleanup after intent resolution. Any boot or installation requires separate immediate system/storage/data-loss approval and a human confirmation gate.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The owner resolves test meaning and destructive boundary; an operator may handle vendor Web UI confirmation. Capability queries, evidence and host device comparisons can be automated; installation judgment/recovery cannot be inferred by the agent.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On unexpected autorun, boot change, installer, device mismatch, loss of console or failed eject, stop all input/writes, preserve state, detach media through the approved path, recover boot/storage under owner control and do not reboot or retry until disposition.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved end state, unsupported/ambiguous transport, unverified image or certificate/auth, non-isolated host, missing console/eject/recovery, unexpected device/content/autorun/boot/install behavior, any unapproved storage write or failed cleanup.

identified_defects: The source contradicts itself on optional OS-install use versus mandatory auto-install appearance, so test completion is not defined.
DeepSeek's lsblk check proves neither exact image content nor transport security and ignores boot/install/storage risk and eject cleanup.
HTTP versus HTTPS and network URL versus local Browse are conflated.
reason_for_change: Preserve V2's genuine semantic BLOCKED conclusion while explicitly identifying the source conflict and the safe read-only/preparatory work that does not constitute testcase completion.

new_technical_evidence.title: DMTF Redfish Data Model Specification — VirtualMedia
new_technical_evidence.version: 2025.2; applicable only if implemented by the tested BMC
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Standards-based virtual-media semantic reference, not a substitute for the OpenBMC vendor flow
new_technical_evidence.supports: InsertMedia attaches remote media from an Image URI and makes it inserted/host-visible; EjectMedia detaches it and clears inserted/image state. Neither action defines or authorizes OS installation.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The BMC's actual schema/support, certificate behavior, web workflow and the source's auto-install intent remain unresolved.

removed_ambiguities: Separates media attachment/visibility from booting or installing.
Makes the procedure-versus-criterion conflict a formal SOURCE_CONFLICT rather than a generic missing-input note.
Defines safe discovery/preparation that cannot be misreported as completion.
resolved_blockers: The reversible mount substage and safe pre-work are technically understandable, but resolving them does not unblock the full conflicting testcase.
remaining_blockers: The whole case remains BLOCKED until the owner resolves mount-only versus installer behavior and provides the matching image/transport/target/cleanup/recovery contract.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 keeps V2's justified BLOCKED verdict, formally identifies SOURCE_CONFLICT, and prevents safe capability discovery or even a successful mount from being mistaken for completion of an undefined auto-install requirement.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The genuine semantic blocker and mount-versus-install boundary are queued for isolated validation.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source combines OpenBMC HTTP virtual-media mounting with a criterion that an undefined Auto-install program appears under the server system.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 correctly identifies the semantic/destructive split; V3 adds a formal SOURCE_CONFLICT and safe-substage-versus-completion distinction.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: No media insertion or boot/install action while intent conflicts; only capability/baseline/image-metadata pre-work is allowed, and installation requires a separate disk/data-loss contract.
